overview: The railway made worth building: faster track that switches itself, a handbrake for the rider, carts chained into trains, and working carts that lay track and dig.

1.2.0: Rails go on walls and ceilings. Held against a wall a rail climbs it if you look up or down as you place it, or runs along it if you look level; held against the underside of a block it hangs from the ceiling. Held against another rail it is still a floor rail, so bridges build as before.
A floor rail under the foot of a climb bends up onto the wall, and the top of a climb bends over onto a ceiling rail beside it, so floor, wall, ceiling and back down is a loop.

Carts ride all of it: slowing up a climb and rolling back if they run out of speed, upside down under a ceiling at any speed, and stopping at the end of a line. A powered rail on a climb lifts a cart from a standstill, and a minecart can be set down on wall or ceiling track.
On Pandorical clients carts on wall and ceiling track are drawn upside down or on end with their riders, and a rider's view turns too unless switched off in Pandorical's settings.
The handbrake works on wall and ceiling track, a furnace cart pushes itself up a wall at full throttle, and dropper and dispenser carts wait for the floor to work.
1.1.11: Describes itself in one short line of what it adds.
1.1.10: A chain between carts shows again after its carts' chunk reloads, and a held chain only tells watchers when it is shown or put away.
A broken cart, a player leaving with a cart panel open, and a closed world leave nothing of theirs behind in the server's memory.
1.1.9: A demo to play in PvP Dimensions' onboarding.
1.1.8: Drop changelog notes for changes nothing in the game shows.
1.1.4: An advancement for the first real tunnel bored with a train of TNT carts.
1.1.3: A chain of TNT carts goes off as one charge and bores a corridor you can walk down.
Rail laid ahead spans drops and follows a climb instead of stopping.
Chained carts hold one speed along the link.
A cart with a heading wears an arrow that says which way it is pointed.
1.0.0: Speed lives in the track, and rails switch themselves.
The rider gets a handbrake, and carts couple into trains.
Three of the working carts become tools that lay track or dig.
